transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM), Dana Rowe (LumenForge Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (SRE), Jamal Brooks (Product)

Summary: quick QBR-style health check focused on adoption ramp, cost trajectory, SLA forecasting and a potential Dedicated pilot. Discussed right-sizing, KV/prefix cache impact, VPC/on-prem constraints, SOC2 controls and next steps to run a short benchmark.

Topics: adoption metrics, cost drivers, latency hotspots, SLA targets, pilot scope, compliance docs

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Looks like we have most folks, great. Today is a short QBR, focus on adoption bridge and SLA forecasting. Dana, you wanna kick us off on what changed since last quarter?
[00:22] Dana Rowe: Yeah sure, um, thanks Maya. So adoption is up, we moved from alpha to beta in a few product flows. Token volume increased, like, around 2.8x during checkout chat, which is great, but that also bumped our bill and some tail latency issues at peak.
[00:40] Jamal Brooks: The product team saw some errors during midnight rollouts, like timeouts. Not sure if those are infra or model.
[00:50] Ethan Cole: Right, Ethan from Redwood SE here — that's usually where continuous batching and KV cache interplay shows up. If prefix cache is cold at rollouts you'll see a bigger spike.
[01:08] Priya Nair: We saw CPU contention on the orchestrator and a lot of retry storms. We are on a VPC peering setup with private endpoints, but bursting is limited.
[01:22] Ravi Singh: From a CSM standpoint, sounds like cost and reliability are converging risks. Let's map SLOs and see if Dedicated or reserved capacity helps.
[01:31] Dana Rowe: Our stakeholders want a 99.9% p95 at peak and cost per 1k tokens to drop by 25% in three months.
[01:40] Maya Patel: Okay, good, realistic. We'll talk tradeoffs: reserved capacity buys predictability but you lose some flexibility; hosted with smarter routing and quantization can hit cost goals but might need model variant testing.
[02:02] Carlos Mendez: Quick question — encryption & KMS: if we go Dedicated in our VPC, does Redwood integrate with our HSM? We have strict KMS policies.
[02:13] Ethan Cole: Yes — we support KMS/HSM integrations. There's an on-prem key wrapping pattern we use. We'll share the security checklist.
[02:26] Priya Nair: And audit logs — we need immutable logs for at least 1 year for compliance.
[02:33] Maya Patel: That's in our add-on compliance package; we can include long-term log retention and export to your SIEM. We'll drop the SOC2 and ISO docs in the follow-up.
[02:45] Jamal Brooks: On the latency side, can you explain the difference between dedicated GPU pools and your smart routing fallback? We want graceful degradation when a model is down.
[02:58] Ethan Cole: Sure — Dedicated gives you a pinned pool so cold starts are predictable, batching is controlled. Smart routing is policy-based: route low-latency requests to smaller quantized variants, fall back to hosted versions or other regions if capacity constrained. You can configure automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[03:20] Dana Rowe: How often do you see quality regressions with quantized models? We can't risk hallucinations for checkout flows.
[03:29] Ethan Cole: Good point. For most open models we validate against your eval sets first. Quantization sometimes reduces rare-token fidelity; we recommend canary rollouts and model-level eval suites.
[03:43] Carlos Mendez: We have a sensitive customers segment — can we have per-tenant routing rules?
[03:51] Maya Patel: Yes, route by token tags or tenant id; we can pin certain tenants to Dedicated and others to cost-optimized hosted.
[04:00] Dana Rowe: Great. Okay — let's get into numbers: our token breakouts and where costs are happening. Carlos, you had telemetry?
[04:10] Carlos Mendez: I pulled aggregated token-level usage for two weeks — peaks at 4.2M tokens per hour during afternoon window. Most cost is generative tokens from chat and the long-context retrieval flow. I'll send aggregate files after the call.
[04:24] Ethan Cole: Awesome — with that profile we can estimate batching gains. If you enable prefix/KV cache and 100ms batching window we'd expect a 20-35% cost reduction on gen-heavy routes, depending on reuse.
[04:40] Priya Nair: That 100ms is too aggressive for checkout — we need sub-50ms latency for p50.
[04:47] Ethan Cole: Right — you can do hybrid: low-latency routes with tiny batches, background flows with larger batching. We'll show suggested per-route configs.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Let's talk SLA forecasting — what does 99.9% p95 look like with your current peak?
[05:07] Ravi Singh: If we assume current hosted profile and no Dedicated, hitting 99.9% p95 at peak is possible but costs may rise ~30% due to overprovisioning to avoid queueing. Dedicated with modest reserve can meet SLA with ~12-18% unit-cost increase but better predictability.
[05:28] Dana Rowe: So Dedicated cuts variance but still costs more than optimizing the model? Which to prioritize?
[05:36] Maya Patel: A typical path is: small Dedicated commit for critical tenants + aggressive caching and quantization on non-critical flows. That hybrid usually hits both cost and SLA objectives.
[05:46] Jamal Brooks: Any examples from other customers?
[05:50] Ethan Cole: One merchant — they used a 2 GPU Dedicated buffer for checkout spikes, plus hosted fallback. Latency SLOs improved and cost per 1k tokens dropped 18% after 8 weeks of caching tuning.
[06:05] Dana Rowe: Okay interesting. On the security side, can we get a diagram of network flows for private deployment?
[06:12] Maya Patel: We'll attach an architecture diagram. For VPC/private we do egress-controlled peering and can run the control plane in your tenancy if needed.
[06:20] Carlos Mendez: We need to validate the burst policy — currently our peering blocks large egress bursts.
[06:26] Priya Nair: And also the onsite MTT (mean time to)? We had a 45-minute incident last month — need to reduce that.
[06:33] Ravi Singh: We can propose an on-call runbook and 24/7 support for Enterprise tiers; that shortens MTTR significantly.
[06:40] Dana Rowe: Good — let's align on the runbook.

[07:00] -- (mid-call, demo artifacts referenced) --
[07:02] Maya Patel: I'm going to share a link to the right-sizing worksheet in chat: (link: https://redwood.app/secure/right-sizing-lumenforge) — note: internal doc, short-lived link.
[07:18] Jamal Brooks: Received. I also opened the benchmark template.

[08:05] Ethan Cole: On bench specifics, for the KV/prefix cache pilot we need a representative 24-hour trace, not PII — sanitized. We want to run: cold-start series, steady-state, and a spike window. The benchmark will compare: hosted baseline, hosted + cache, dedicated buffer + cache.
[08:28] Carlos Mendez: We can produce the trace but need guidance on sanitization.
[08:33] Ethan Cole: We'll share a sanitization script.

[09:10] Priya Nair: About cost allocation — we want per-route token breakdown in our billing. Is that possible?
[09:16] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console can break down token-level cost by route and model. You can export CSV for your internal FinOps.

[10:00] Dana Rowe: Quick tangent — competitors. We evaluated LambdaCloud and ScaleServe. LambdaCloud seemed cheaper for bulk embeddings but had poor reliability at peak. ScaleServe had better SLAs but closed ecosystem. Does Redwood have similar embedding discounts?
[10:18] Maya Patel: We can negotiate committed volume discounts for embeddings and propose a hybrid routing to use a cheaper model for large batch embeddings where quality allows.

[11:00] Ethan Cole: One more technical note — KV cache hits are sensitive to prompt templating. If your product inserts user-specific noise at the front, cache effectiveness drops. We recommend normalized prompt prefixes for high-reuse flows.
[11:18] Jamal Brooks: Hmm, we do personalize prompts early — we'll run a lint pass to standardize prefixes.

[12:05] -- (analysis segment: cost modeling) --
[12:07] Ethan Cole: With the telemetry you provided, initial modeling suggests two levers: reduce tokens via prompt engineering (8-12% savings) and increase cache hit from 15% to 45% (another 25-30% savings). Combined it's plausible to meet the 25% cost reduction target without full Dedicated.
[12:34] Priya Nair: But that needs product changes which take time. We need a short-term fix.
[12:41] Maya Patel: Short-term: small Dedicated buffer + quick caching tuning for the highest-volume route. Medium-term: quantization on non-critical flows and prompt rework.

[13:10] -- (risk and compliance) --
[13:12] Dana Rowe: Can you confirm data residency options? We have EU customers and need to keep tokens in EU.
[13:19] Maya Patel: Yes — region pinning and private deployments available. Also can do on-prem package for very strict customers.

[14:00] Carlos Mendez: On billing, we need to map current spend to projected spend across three scenarios: baseline, caching/optimizations, and Dedicated hybrid. Can Redwood produce that?
[14:08] Maya Patel: We'll produce a 3-scenario projection with assumptions. I'll send it with the pricing tiers.

[28:00] -- (deep-dive interlude with SE) --
[28:10] Ethan Cole: About canaries and rollback — recommend test traffic at 2% and monitor quality via your eval prompts. We have hooks to auto-fallback on NPD (novelty/perplexity) thresholds.
[28:30] Jamal Brooks: Sounds good. We need a standard evaluation harness — do you provide one?
[28:36] Ethan Cole: Yes, Redwood Optimize has an eval suite; we can onboard your prompt set and run regressions.

[37:45] -- (action summary and wrap) --
[37:50] Ravi Singh: Quick recap: Redwood to run bench plan, LumenForge to provide telemetry and sanitized trace, Redwood to send pricing + compliance docs, SRE and Product to align on prompt normalization.
[38:06] Dana Rowe: Yep, that matches. We also want the architecture diagram and runbook.
[38:12] Maya Patel: All right, specific due dates and owners in the action items — Ethan will run bench, Carlos will provide data, Maya will send pricing and docs, Priya to confirm compliance contacts.
[38:25] Priya Nair: One last thing — can we try a 2-week pilot with a 2-GPU Dedicated buffer and automatic fallback to hosted during peak? If it shows MTTR improvements we'll scale.
[38:36] Maya Patel: We can set that up as a pilot. I'll include a pilot T&C in the follow up.
[38:42] Jamal Brooks: Thanks everyone. Clear next steps.
[38:47] Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up in writing by end of day tomorrow with the doc links and a timeline.

[52:55] -- meeting end --

Notes and references: shared right-sizing spreadsheet link above, benchmark template (link shared in chat), SOC2+ISO docs to be shared via secure portal.

Explicit next steps (verbatim from call):
- Send tailored right-sizing proposal and pricing tiers by 2027-08-10.
- Share SOC2 + ISO and on-prem deployment checklist via secure link.
- Schedule 1-week pilot for KV cache benchmark (Redwood to run bench once sanitized trace provided).
- Provide architecture diagram and on-call runbook for Dedicated pilot.

Potential risks called out: need for prompt normalization to get cache benefits; KMS/HSM integration validation; peering/burst policy constraints; timeline for product-level prompt changes.

Questions raised (to follow up):
- Can Redwood export per-route token billing in a format ingestible by our FinOps? (Answer: yes, CSV export available).
- Does deduped caching affect user personalization? (Answer: caching is prefix-aware; we can scope per-route).

End of transcript.
